note: A screen, not an audit: questions worth asking and the data needed to answer them. No savings are computed; typical benefits are the cited sources' general wording.

questions.question: Does a temperature controller write straight to a steam valve with no flow controller underneath (a cascade candidate)?

evidence.text: valve TV-A reads "TV-A STEAM valve" at U-A
controller TIC-A reads "TIC-A Fictional supplied controller" at U-A
instrument FT-A reads "FT-A STEAM flow" at U-A
no flow controller between the temperature controller and the valve

where: DCS/PLC configuration: controller tuning and output history
data_requests.how: Look for oscillation or slow recovery after steam pressure changes.

where: site records: steam header pressure trend
data_requests.how: Note how often supply pressure moves.

questions.decision_rule: A flow slave helps when steam supply pressure swings disturb the temperature; a steady header and a well-behaved loop close this screening investigation.

typical_benefit.wording: No public numeric source found. Report as qualitative only.

questions.limits: Also covers heating and cooling valves on one exchanger with separate controllers that could fight; that pattern is not detected automatically yet.
